edits.old: Do not interpret Percona's claim of identical analytics data as guaranteed identical operation coverage. A level-2 database profiler captures all operations, while the documented mongolog example logs operations beyond its threshold. MongoDB profiling filters can instead control which operations enter both outputs and override slowms and sampleRate. Coverage must be compared under the actual configurations. (high confidence)
edits.new: Do not interpret Percona's claim of identical analytics data as guaranteed identical operation coverage. A level-2 database profiler collects data for all operations, while the documented mongolog example sets mode: off with slowOpThresholdMs: 100, so only slow operations are logged. On mongod, a MongoDB profiling filter affects both the diagnostic log and the profiler, and when a filter is set slowms and sampleRate do not affect either. Coverage must be compared under the actual configurations. Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/install-pmm/install-pmm-client/connect-database/mongodb.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/

edits.rationale: The Percona and MongoDB pages support the claim's statements. The original phrasing of the filter statement is loose. MongoDB says a filter set on mongod affects both the diagnostic log and the profiler, and that slowms and sampleRate then have no effect. Separately, level 2 ignores user-provided slowms and filter, so filters do not override level 2.
